title: ETS Legacy Network Syslog Hardware Qualification Profile
purpose: Apply the common ETS HQP contract to a physical legacy network device observed through the existing ETS Edge RFC 5424 UDP syslog boundary without upgrading transport observations into authenticated source identity.
product_scope: Legacy hardware lab / RFC 5424 UDP network source

capability_boundary.claim_statement: Qualification applies only to the named legacy source device/firmware, observer adapter build, transport configuration, and retained test evidence. UDP source address and RFC 5424 identity fields remain observations rather than authenticated identity.

device_constraints.notes: The source device is qualified only as the exact named legacy hardware/firmware target. Observer-side Edge hardware and software are separately bound in build/environment evidence.

test_cases.title: Bind legacy source and observer configuration
test_cases.purpose: Retain exact physical source hardware/firmware, configured syslog identity, observer adapter build, interface, transport, and time-source facts before traffic tests execute.
pass_criteria: Manufacturer/model/revision/firmware and configured syslog identity are retained for the source device.
Observer Edge build, network interface, UDP listener configuration, packet-observation method, and time source are retained separately from source claims.
test_cases.safety_boundary: Use an isolated lab network and preserve the source configuration before making test changes.

test_cases.title: Commit exact received RFC 5424 datagram bytes
test_cases.purpose: Prove that a physical legacy source can emit a datagram whose exact received bytes are committed before parsing and are independently reviewable through ETS evidence.
pass_criteria: The observer hashes the exact received datagram bytes before parsing.
Bounded RFC 5424 metadata and source IP/port observations are retained without copying raw MSG or structured-data content into default metadata stores.
The committed event/proof can be independently verified without trusting the source device.
test_cases.safety_boundary: Use synthetic/non-sensitive syslog content and do not expose the UDP listener outside the controlled lab network.

test_cases.title: Preserve unauthenticated source-identity boundary
test_cases.purpose: Demonstrate that UDP source address and RFC 5424 identity fields remain transport/message observations and are never upgraded into authenticated device identity.
pass_criteria: The qualification package explicitly records UDP as unauthenticated transport for this profile.
No source IP, port, hostname, app-name, procid, or msgid field is represented as cryptographically authenticated source identity.
test_cases.safety_boundary: Do not add credentials or production trust assertions merely to make the legacy source appear stronger than its actual transport.

test_cases.title: One-byte datagram mutation produces a distinct commitment
test_cases.purpose: Demonstrate substitution detection for observed legacy-device messages without claiming that either message is semantically true.
pass_criteria: Changing any retained test datagram byte changes the received-byte SHA-256 commitment.
Original and mutated observations remain distinct Evidence Object/event references.
test_cases.safety_boundary: Use test messages; do not mutate production traffic or operational device logs.

test_cases.title: Observer restart preserves committed legacy-source evidence
test_cases.purpose: Exercise the existing Edge persistence boundary while keeping the legacy source device as the DUT under observation.
pass_criteria: An acknowledged committed record from the physical source remains recoverable after observer restart.
Independent proof verification succeeds after restart without consulting the source device's runtime state.
test_cases.safety_boundary: Restart only the designated lab observer/adapter and preserve storage before destructive diagnostics.

test_cases.title: Source or network interruption does not fabricate history
test_cases.purpose: Bound missing-observation behavior when the legacy source or network path is interrupted and prove clean resumption without backfilling invented events.
pass_criteria: The package distinguishes no observation from evidence that no source event occurred.
No synthetic success event is created to fill the interruption window.
Post-recovery capture resumes as a new observation with the interruption boundary retained.
test_cases.safety_boundary: Perform interruption testing on an isolated test path and restore the original source/network configuration afterward.
